This markdown reproduces the panels of **Figure 3**. We project the
RIG-I-only and STAT-only (IFN-only) signatures, derived from the A549
bulk model in Figure 1, onto the single-cell RNA-Seq data of nasal
swabs from SARS-CoV-2 positive and negative children and adults
published by
[Loske et al. 2021, Nat. Biotechnol.](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41587-021-01037-9).
Every cell is scored with both signatures (Seurat `AddModuleScore`), and
cells are classified into two quadrants of the RIG-I-only vs STAT-only
score plane using thresholds derived from SARS-CoV-2 negative donors
(99.959 % quantile of the RIG-I-only score and 99.99 % quantile of the
STAT-only score of all cells of SARS-CoV-2 negative donors):

* **Quadrant I**: RIG-I-only score above threshold and STAT-only score
  below threshold (cells with direct RIG-I activity but no IFN-receptor
  signalling).
* **Quadrant II**: STAT-only score above threshold and RIG-I-only score
  below threshold (bystander cells responding to secreted IFN).

Panels produced (all saved in `figures/figure_03/`):

| Panel file | Content |
|---|---|
| `gathering_loske_dataset.pdf` | RIG-I-only vs STAT-only scores of all cells, split by SARS-CoV-2 status and coloured by quadrant |
| `barplots_cell_types_qII.pdf` | Cell-type composition of quadrant I, quadrant II and all cells of SARS-CoV-2 positive donors, with the Fisher-test (BH-adjusted) p-value for enrichment of each cell type in quadrant I |
| `scatterplot_rig_vs_stat_selected_cell_types.pdf` | RIG-I-only vs STAT-only scores of cells carrying SARS-CoV-2 transcripts in selected cell types, coloured by viral load |
| `neutrophils_features_scov2pos.pdf` | RIG-I-only vs STAT-only scores of neutrophils carrying SARS-CoV-2 transcripts coloured by viral load, age group and IFNL1 expression |

The code was taken from the original analysis script
`/media/ag-cherrmann/cramirez/interferon_model/scripts/R/july_2026/03_scRNASeq_projections_loske.Rmd`
(which wrote these panels to `figures/2026_May/` on 2026-10-01), except
for the cell-type barplot (`barplots_cell_types_qII.pdf`), which was produced
on 2026-05-18 by an earlier version of
`/media/ag-cherrmann/cramirez/interferon_model/scripts/R/may_2026/03_scRNASeq_projections_loske.Rmd`
(see the section *Cell-type composition of the quadrants* for details).
Only the code needed for these panels was kept; plotting code, PDF sizes
and aesthetics are unchanged.

The neutrophil subset defined at the end of this markdown (SARS-CoV-2
transcript-positive neutrophils used for the children vs adults
comparison) is saved to `analysis/figure_03/` and is the input of
`supplementary_figure_03.Rmd` (volcano plot and GSEA), so **this markdown
has to be run before `supplementary_figure_03.Rmd`**.


# Input data

| Input | Absolute path / source |
|---|---|
| Processed Seurat object of the nasal-swab scRNA-Seq data (raw counts, normalised data, UMAP and cell annotation as published by the authors; file `210716_figshare_upload_ag_lehmann.rds` downloaded from the figshare repository of Loske et al. 2021 (see the Data availability section of the [paper](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41587-021-01037-9))). Viral transcripts are included as features `SARS-CoV-2-p` (positive strand) and `SARS-CoV-2-m` (minus strand) | `/media/bq-storage/ag-cherrmann/cramirez/data/loske_2021/210716_figshare_upload_ag_lehmann.rds` |
| Cell metadata used (columns of the Seurat object above, as provided by Loske et al.) | `detailed_clusters` (cell type), `covid` (SARS-CoV-2 status of the donor: `pos` / `neg`), `covid_kid1` (status x age group: `pos_adult`, `pos_children`, `neg_adult`, `neg_children`), `dps` (days post symptom onset) |
| Viral load per cell | `SARS-CoV-2-p` expression (normalised data of the Seurat object above) |
| RIG-I-only / STAT-only signatures (written by `figure_01.Rmd`) | `/media/bq-storage/ag-cherrmann/cramirez/decoupling_rigi_ifn/analysis/figure_01/rigi_vs_stat_only_signatures.rds` (`path2signs` in `settings.R`) |
| Shared settings (paths, colours) | `/media/bq-storage/ag-cherrmann/cramirez/decoupling_rigi_ifn/scripts/R/settings.R` |

No MSigDB gene sets are used for the panels of this figure.


```{r dependencies, results='hide', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(Seurat)
library(gridExtra)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(colorspace)

source("/media/bq-storage/ag-cherrmann/cramirez/decoupling_rigi_ifn/scripts/R/settings.R")
```


## Initial settings

Output folders of this section (`figures/figure_03/` and
`analysis/figure_03/` in the repository).

```{r setting_up}
dirs <- section_dirs("figure_03")
path2figures <- dirs$figures
path2analysis <- dirs$analysis
```


## Loading the data from Loske et al. 2021

Processed Seurat object as published by the authors on figshare. The
object already contains normalised data and the cell annotation, so no
further processing is needed.

```{r loading_loske}
path2loske <- '/media/bq-storage/ag-cherrmann/cramirez/data/loske_2021/210716_figshare_upload_ag_lehmann.rds'
seurat <- readRDS(path2loske)
seurat
```

Overview of the metadata columns used in this figure and confirmation that
the viral transcripts are features of the object.

```{r metadata_overview}
table(seurat$covid, useNA = 'ifany')
table(seurat$covid_kid1, useNA = 'ifany')
table(seurat$dps, useNA = 'ifany')
table(seurat$detailed_clusters, useNA = 'ifany')
c('SARS-CoV-2-p', 'SARS-CoV-2-m') %in% rownames(seurat)
```


## Loading signatures

RIG-I-only and STAT-only signatures defined in Figure 1. As in the original
analysis, interferon genes (IFNB / IFNL) are removed from the signatures
before scoring, and the list is reordered as (`stat_only`, `rigi_only`), so
that `AddModuleScore` names the scores `stat_only1` and `rigi_only2`.

```{r loading_signatures}
signatures <- readRDS(path2signs)
signatures <- lapply(signatures,
                     function(genes){
                             genes[!grepl('IFNB|IFNL', genes)]
})
signatures <- signatures[c(2,1)]
str(signatures)
```


## Scoring cells

Module scores of both signatures for every cell (`AddModuleScore` uses a
fixed seed by default, so scores are reproducible).

```{r scoring_cells}
seurat <- AddModuleScore(seurat,
                         features = signatures,
                         name = names(signatures))

seurat@meta.data %>% colnames
```


## Selected cell types (panel `scatterplot_rig_vs_stat_selected_cell_types.pdf`)

RIG-I-only vs STAT-only scores of cells with SARS-CoV-2 (+) strand
transcripts (`SARS-CoV-2-p > 0`) in nine selected cell types, coloured by
the viral load. Donors at 10-12 days post symptoms are excluded.

```{r selected_cell_types, fig.width=8, fig.height=7}
df_signatures <- FetchData(seurat, c('stat_only1',
                                     'rigi_only2',
                                     'covid',
                                     'dps',
                                     'detailed_clusters',
                                     'SARS-CoV-2-p',
                                     'SARS-CoV-2-m')) %>%
        dplyr::filter(!dps %in% c('10', '11', '12')) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(dps = factor(dps, sort(unique(dps))))


selected_cells <- c("nrMa",
                "Neutrophil",
                "moMa",
                "Squamous",
                "Epi_lowRNA",
                "CD11c_mDC",
                "NK",
                "Cil_acute_phase",
                "pDC")
p_all <- df_signatures %>%
        dplyr::filter(`SARS-CoV-2-p` > 0) %>%
        arrange(`SARS-CoV-2-p`) %>%
        filter(detailed_clusters %in% selected_cells) %>%
        mutate(detailed_clusters = factor(detailed_clusters,
                                          levels = selected_cells)) %>%
ggplot(aes(x = rigi_only2,
                          y = stat_only1,
                          colour = `SARS-CoV-2-p`)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = 'dashed') +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.0, linetype = 'dashed') +
  facet_wrap(  ~ detailed_clusters) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 3)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 3)) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 12),
    strip.background = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "RIGI-only Score",
    y = "STAT-only Score",
    title = ""
  ) + viridis::scale_color_viridis()


p_all
pdf(paste0(path2figures,
           "/scatterplot_rig_vs_stat_selected_cell_types.pdf"),
    width=8, height=7)
p_all
dev.off()
```


## Virtual gathering (panel `gathering_loske_dataset.pdf`)

Quadrant thresholds are computed from cells of SARS-CoV-2 negative donors
(99.99 % quantile of `stat_only1`, 99.959 % quantile of `rigi_only2`).
Quadrant I: `stat_only1 <= stat_th & rigi_only2 >= rigi_th`; quadrant II:
`stat_only1 >= stat_th & rigi_only2 <= rigi_th`; all other cells are `NA`
(grey). All cells are plotted, split by SARS-CoV-2 status of the donor.

```{r virtual_gathering, fig.width=5, fig.height=2.75}
md <- FetchData(seurat,
                vars = c(colnames(seurat@meta.data),
                         'SARS-CoV-2-p'))

cols <- brewer.pal(4, "Set2")[2:4]
names(cols) <- c("I", "II")

stat_th <- quantile(subset(md, covid == 'neg')$stat_only1, 0.9999)
stat_th
rigi_th <- quantile(subset(md, covid == 'neg')$rigi_only2, 0.99959)
rigi_th

md <-  md %>%
  mutate(
    quadrant = case_when(
      stat_only1 <= stat_th & rigi_only2 >= rigi_th ~ "I",
      stat_only1 >= stat_th & rigi_only2 <= rigi_th   ~ "II",
      FALSE ~ "III"
    )
  )
gathering_loske <- md %>%  ggplot(aes(x = rigi_only2, y = stat_only1, color = quadrant)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1, shape = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = stat_th, linetype = 'dashed') +
  geom_vline(xintercept = rigi_th, linetype = 'dashed') +
  theme_bw() +
        facet_wrap(~covid) +
        scale_colour_manual(values = cols) +
  labs(
    x = "rigi_only2",
    y = "stat_only1",
    color = "Quadrant"
  ) +
        scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1.0))

gathering_loske

pdf(paste0(path2figures,
           '/gathering_loske_dataset.pdf'),
    width=5, height=2.75)
gathering_loske
dev.off()
```


Number of cells per quadrant and SARS-CoV-2 status.

```{r quadrant_counts}
table(md$covid, md$quadrant, useNA = 'ifany')
```


## Cell-type composition of the quadrants (panel `barplots_cell_types_qII.pdf`)

**Provenance of this panel.** The figure panel
`/media/ag-cherrmann/cramirez/interferon_model/figures/2026_May/barplots_cell_types_qII.pdf`
(2026-05-18) was produced by an earlier version of
`/media/ag-cherrmann/cramirez/interferon_model/scripts/R/may_2026/03_scRNASeq_projections_loske.Rmd`.
The current version of that script contains the same plotting code but
labels the "Total" column with a string pasting the quadrant I and quadrant
II FDRs from a separate test (`results_joined`, computed in a later chunk)
and saves the plot as `barplots_cell_types_fdr.pdf` (2026-06-24). Comparing
both PDFs, the bars and percentages are identical, but the qII panel shows
labels of the form `adj.p = 4e-54`, i.e. the `p_label` column built in this
very chunk from the BH-adjusted Fisher-test p-value of enrichment of each
cell type in quadrant I (`padj_I`). Therefore, the code below is the
current `may_2026` code with the label of the p-value text layer set to
`p_label` (data `plot_df`) instead of the FDR string of `plot_df_fdr`;
everything else (bars, colours, sizes, the 7 x 3 inch PDF) is unchanged.
The output is saved under the name of the figure panel,
`barplots_cell_types_qII.pdf`.

Proportions are computed among cells of SARS-CoV-2 positive donors for
all cells ("Total"), quadrant I and quadrant II, keeping the cell types
present in quadrant I. For each cell type, a Fisher's exact test compares
the cell type vs all other cells in quadrant I vs outside quadrant I,
and p-values are BH-adjusted.

```{r barplots_cell_types, fig.width=7, fig.height=3}
# =========================================================
# 1. Compute proportions
# =========================================================

## Preparing the data
# keep only relevant columns
df <- md %>%
  filter(covid == "pos") %>%
  select(detailed_clusters, quadrant)

# total number of cells
n_total <- nrow(df)

prop_total <- df %>%
  count(detailed_clusters) %>%
  mutate(
    group = "Total",
    proportion = n / sum(n)
  )

prop_I <- df %>%
  filter(quadrant == "I") %>%
  count(detailed_clusters) %>%
  mutate(
    group = "I",
    proportion = n / sum(n)
  )

prop_II <- df %>%
  filter(quadrant == "II") %>%
  count(detailed_clusters) %>%
  mutate(
    group = "II",
    proportion = n / sum(n)
  )

props <- bind_rows(
  prop_total,
  prop_I,
  prop_II
)

# =========================================================
# 2. Keep only clusters present in quadrant I
# =========================================================


clusters_keep <- prop_I %>%
  filter(proportion > 0) %>%
  pull(detailed_clusters)

props <- props %>%
  filter(detailed_clusters %in% clusters_keep)

# =========================================================
# 3. Fisher enrichment tests
# =========================================================

df_test <- df

clusters <- unique(props$detailed_clusters)

enrichment_results <- lapply(clusters, function(cl){

  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # Fisher test for Quadrant I enrichment
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  tab_I <- matrix(c(

    # cluster in I
    sum(
      df_test$detailed_clusters == cl &
        df_test$quadrant == "I",
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    # other clusters in I
    sum(
      df_test$detailed_clusters != cl &
        df_test$quadrant == "I",
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    # cluster not in I
    sum(
      df_test$detailed_clusters == cl &
        df_test$quadrant != "I",
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    # other clusters not in I
    sum(
      df_test$detailed_clusters != cl &
        df_test$quadrant != "I",
      na.rm = TRUE
    )

  ),
  nrow = 2,
  byrow = TRUE)

  test_I <- fisher.test(tab_I)

  data.frame(
    detailed_clusters = cl,
    p_I = test_I$p.value,
    OR_I = test_I$estimate
  )

}) %>%
  bind_rows()

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Adjust p-values
# ---------------------------------------------------------

enrichment_results <- enrichment_results %>%
  mutate(
    padj_I = p.adjust(p_I, method = "BH")
  )

# =========================================================
# 4. Merge
# =========================================================

plot_df <- props %>%
  left_join(
    enrichment_results,
    by = "detailed_clusters"
  )

# =========================================================
# 5. Labels
# =========================================================

plot_df <- plot_df %>%
  mutate(

    proportion_pct = round(
      proportion * 100,
      1
    ),

    prop_label = paste0(
      proportion_pct,
      "%"
    ),

    p_label = paste0(
      "adj.p = ",
      signif(padj_I, 2)
    )
  )

# =========================================================
# 6. Order clusters
# =========================================================

cluster_order <- prop_I %>%
  arrange(desc(proportion)) %>%
  pull(detailed_clusters)

plot_df$detailed_clusters <- factor(
  plot_df$detailed_clusters,
  levels = rev(cluster_order)
)

# =========================================================
# 7. TRUE 0-100% SCALE
# =========================================================
# Bars now represent actual percentages
# instead of scaling to group maxima
# =========================================================

plot_df <- plot_df %>%
  mutate(
    scaled_prop = proportion
  )

# =========================================================
# 8. Palette
# =========================================================

n_clusters <- length(
  unique(plot_df$detailed_clusters)
)

pal <- qualitative_hcl(
  n_clusters,
  palette = "Dark 3"
)

names(pal) <- levels(
  plot_df$detailed_clusters
)

# =========================================================
# 9. Plot
# =========================================================

barplots_cell_types <- ggplot(
  plot_df,
  aes(
    x = group,
    y = detailed_clusters
  )
) +

  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # background boxes (100% width)
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  geom_rect(
    aes(
      xmin = as.numeric(factor(group)) - 0.40,
      xmax = as.numeric(factor(group)) + 0.40,

      ymin = as.numeric(detailed_clusters) - 0.33,
      ymax = as.numeric(detailed_clusters) + 0.33
    ),
    fill = "white",
    color = "black",
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +

  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # loading bars
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  geom_rect(
    aes(

      xmin = as.numeric(factor(group)) - 0.40,

      xmax =
        (as.numeric(factor(group)) - 0.40) +
        scaled_prop * 0.80,

      ymin = as.numeric(detailed_clusters) - 0.22,
      ymax = as.numeric(detailed_clusters) + 0.22,

      fill = detailed_clusters
    ),
    color = NA
  ) +

  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # proportion labels
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  geom_text(
    data = subset(plot_df, group == "I"),
    aes(label = prop_label),
    x = 0.58,
    size = 3,
    hjust = 1
  ) +

  geom_text(
    data = subset(plot_df, group == "II"),
    aes(label = prop_label),
    x = 1.58,
    size = 3,
    hjust = 1
  ) +

  geom_text(
    data = subset(plot_df, group == "Total"),
    aes(label = prop_label),
    x = 2.58,
    size = 3,
    hjust = 1
  ) +

  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # p-value labels (quadrant I enrichment, BH-adjusted)
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  geom_text(
    data = subset(plot_df, group == "Total"),
    aes(label = p_label),
    x = 3.08,
    size = 2.6,
    hjust = 0
  ) +

  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # colors
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  scale_fill_manual(values = pal) +

  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # theme
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),

    axis.title = element_blank(),

    legend.position = "none",

    axis.text.x = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 12
    ),

    axis.text.y = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 11
    ),

    panel.background = element_rect(
      fill = "grey96",
      color = NA
    )
  )



pdf(paste0(path2figures,
           '/barplots_cell_types_qII.pdf'),
    width=7.0, height=3.0)
barplots_cell_types
dev.off()

barplots_cell_types
```

The proportions and the Fisher-test results behind the panel are saved

## Neutrophils of SARS-CoV-2 positive donors (panel `neutrophils_features_scov2pos.pdf`)

Neutrophils carrying SARS-CoV-2 transcripts (`SARS-CoV-2-p > 0` or
`SARS-CoV-2-m > 0`) from SARS-CoV-2 positive donors (10-12 days post
symptoms excluded). RIG-I-only vs STAT-only scores coloured by
(left) viral load (`SARS-CoV-2-p`), (middle) age group (`covid_kid1`)
and (right) IFNL1 expression.

```{r neutrophils_features, fig.height=4.0, fig.width=14}
df_signatures <- FetchData(seurat, c('stat_only1',
                                     'rigi_only2',
                                     'covid',
                                     'dps',
                                     'detailed_clusters',
                                     'SARS-CoV-2-p',
                                     'SARS-CoV-2-m',
                                     'covid_kid1',
                                     'OASL',
                                     'IFNL1')) %>%
        dplyr::filter(!dps %in% c('10', '11', '12')) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(dps = factor(dps, sort(unique(dps))))

neu_sarscov2 <- df_signatures %>%
        dplyr::filter(`SARS-CoV-2-p` > 0 |
                              `SARS-CoV-2-m` > 0) %>%
        dplyr::filter( ! covid_kid1 %in% c('neg_adult',
                                        'neg_children')) %>%
        dplyr::filter(detailed_clusters %in% c(
                                        'Neutrophil') ) %>%
        arrange(`SARS-CoV-2-p`) %>%
 ggplot(aes(x = rigi_only2,
                          y = stat_only1,
                          colour = `SARS-CoV-2-p`)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 3) +
        viridis::scale_color_viridis() +

    title = ""
  )

gridExtra::grid.arrange(neu_sarscov2,
                        neu_stage,
                        neu_ifnl, ncol = 3)


pdf(paste0(path2figures,
           '/neutrophils_features_scov2pos.pdf'),
    height=4.0, width=14)
gridExtra::grid.arrange(neu_sarscov2,
                        neu_stage,
                        neu_ifnl, ncol = 3)
dev.off()
```


## Neutrophil subset for the children vs adults comparison (input of Supplementary Figure 3)

Same neutrophils as above, excluding children neutrophils with low
RIG-I-only score (`rigi_only2 < 0.5`) and all neutrophils with
`stat_only1 >= 0.25`, as in the original analysis. This subset is the
input of the differential expression analysis (children vs adults) in
`supplementary_figure_03.Rmd`, and is saved to
`analysis/figure_03/seurat_neutrophils_scov2pos_children_vs_adults.rds`.

```{r neutrophil_subset, fig.width=5.5, fig.height=4}
selected_cells <- df_signatures %>%
        dplyr::filter(`SARS-CoV-2-p` > 0 |
                              `SARS-CoV-2-m` > 0) %>%
        dplyr::filter( ! covid_kid1 %in% c('neg_adult',
                                        'neg_children')) %>%
        dplyr::filter(detailed_clusters %in% c(
                                        'Neutrophil') )  %>%
        dplyr::filter( ! ( rigi_only2 < 0.5 &
                                  covid_kid1 == 'pos_children' ) ) %>%
        rownames()


seurat_subset <- seurat[, selected_cells]
seurat_subset <- subset(seurat_subset, stat_only1 < 0.25)

seurat_subset$covid_kid1 %>% table

saveRDS(seurat_subset,
        file = paste0(path2analysis,
                      "/seurat_neutrophils_scov2pos_children_vs_adults.rds"))
```
